newsitem.title: USA: Fujitsu to buy rest of Amdahl for $850 mln.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu to buy rest of Amdahl for $850 mln.

text.p: Japanese computer conglomerate Fujitsu Ltd Wednesday said it will buy the shares of Amdahl Corp. it does not already own for $12 a share, in a cash deal worth about $850 million.
Fujitsu already owns 42 percent of Amdahl, the Sunnyvale, Calif.-based maker of IBM-compatible mainframe computers and related data storage systems.

Fujitsu said Amdahl will become a wholly-owned subsidiary. Its company name and management team will be retained, and there will be essentially no reductions in employment levels as a result of the merger, Fujitsu said.

Amdahl was founded in the early-1970s by Gene Amdahl, the principal architect of International Business Machine Corp.'s popular family of business mainframe computers known as the System 360. The company was the first to offer an alternative mainframe computer, based on IBM-compatible standards, and achieved success by offering machines that were faster, cheaper and with higher capacity than IBM mainframes.
Fujitsu, the world's second largest computer company after IBM, was one of Amdahl's earliest investors, and its stake in the company has steadily grown over the past 25 years.

Amdahl results began to deteriorate in the early 1990s amid a general slowing of demand for mainframe computers, but have stabilised in recent years as it diversified into new product lines and participated in a cut-throat pricing war that spurred new demand for mainframes.
Amdahl stock rose 6.25 cents to $11.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
